papers.title: The impact of behavioural activity on the EEG power spectrum, its source localisation, and global functional connectivity in rats Behavioural modulation of rat EEG dynamics.
papers.summary: Analyzed multichannel ECoG from 116 waking recordings in 12 Wistar rats to isolate behavioral activity effects on EEG power, source localization, and global functional connectivity. Behavioral activity increased 6-8 Hz power (peaking at 7 Hz over parietal/temporal cortex), increased gamma/high-gamma power, decreased delta and beta/high-beta power, with subcortical changes mainly in the thalamus; alpha band was unaffected.

papers.title: Neuronal ensembles in visual cortex reactivate during hypnagogic sleep onset
papers.summary: Using two-photon imaging of rodent visual cortex, the study found that neuronal ensembles activated by visual stimuli or locomotion show increased reactivation specifically during NREM1 sleep onset after prolonged visual stimulation. Ensembles defined during visual stimulus periods were already present before stimulation, suggesting an endogenous cortical lexicon.

papers.title: The bidirectional relationship between epilepsy and sleep: a narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes the bidirectional relationship between epilepsy and sleep disorders, covering neurobiological mechanisms, clinical implications, and therapeutic consequences. It highlights that NREM sleep promotes epileptiform discharges while REM sleep is protective, and that sleep disturbances lower seizure threshold; targeting sleep disturbances may improve seizure control and quality of life.

papers.title: Effects of an 18-month meditation training on subjective and objective sleep quality in older adults: a secondary analysis of the Age-Well randomized controlled trial
papers.summary: Secondary analysis of the Age-Well randomized controlled trial examined whether 18 months of meditation training affected subjective and objective sleep in 120 cognitively unimpaired older adults. Meditation training was associated only with greater ease of morning awakening versus passive control; no significant effects were found on actigraphy or polysomnography measures.

papers.title: Robust information transfer calculation reveals dynamic networks during sleep arousal.
papers.summary: Introduces a robust information-transfer method based on optimized embedding parameters for transfer entropy and applies it to 8,136 sleep arousals from 1,956 subjects in the SHHS follow-up. The max. TE method gave 17.9% more stable estimates than the second-best approach; TE was lower in cardiovascular disease patients than healthy controls, decreased with age, and was highest during REM sleep.

papers.title: What can narcolepsy teach us about hypocretin and dementia?
papers.summary: Reviews whether narcolepsy type 1 and hypocretin loss inform the link between sleep-wake disruption and dementia, noting that biomarker and neuroimaging findings do not consistently support premature brain aging in NT1. Discusses hypocretin interactions with inflammation, metabolism, synaptic plasticity, amyloid processing, circadian organization, and wake-related neuronal activity as possible mechanisms.

papers.title: Hyperexcitable but seizure-free: hippocampal network dysfunction in a Wolfram syndrome model
papers.summary: This study characterized hippocampal function in mice carrying a patient-orthologous Wfs1 p.W542* variant and found that dissociated hippocampal neurons were hyperexcitable but showed no increase in network bursting or criticality shift. In vivo, mutant mice exhibited no epileptiform activity or seizures, with male-specific reduced low-gamma power, sex-specific sleep disruption, impaired fear memory, and reduced voluntary motor activity.

papers.title: Highly stretchable, hair-compatible multichannel neural interface with time-stable hydrogel for high-fidelity long-term EEG sensing.
papers.summary: Presents MindStretcH, a stretchable hair-compatible EEG platform integrating a kirigami-patterned elastomeric mesh, deformable EGaIn interconnects, and detachable hydrogel conical electrodes. Longitudinal motor-imagery recordings and repeated online BCI experiments showed consistent task-related EEG activity without measurable deterioration in recording quality.

papers.title: Obstructive sleep apnea severity associates with reduced phase-lag index functional connectivity during N2 sleep.
papers.summary: In 50 patients with OSA or primary snoring, retrospective polysomnography analysis found that higher apnea-hypopnea index was associated with lower delta-band and theta-band phase-lag index functional connectivity specifically during N2 sleep, while conventional spectral measures showed no significant correlations in any stage.

papers.title: 40 Hz Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation Enhances Verbal Free Recall in Healthy Adults by Modulating Frontal Theta Oscillations.
papers.summary: In a randomized, single-blind, sham-controlled study of 44 healthy young adults, 40 Hz transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation improved verbal free recall compared to sham and 20 Hz stimulation, and increased frontal theta power immediately after stimulation. Frontal theta activity and stimulation-induced theta changes positively correlated with recall performance, supporting a theta-dependent mechanism.

papers.title: Waveform sharpness identifies the morphological phenotype of high-frequency oscillation-associated spikes in pediatric focal epilepsy.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: In a retrospective analysis of 993 interictal spikes from 20 children with focal epilepsy, waveform sharpness (steepness) was the strongest independent morphological correlate of high-frequency oscillation (HFO) presence, with an adjusted odds ratio of 7.41 per 1-SD increase in mixed-effects models. Sharpness distinguished HFO-associated spikes from non-HFO spikes in all patients and may serve as a practical scalp EEG marker.

papers.title: REM sleep EEG slowing signals basal forebrain integrity in older adults with subjective and mild cognitive impairment
papers.summary: In 116 older adults with cognitive concerns, greater REM sleep EEG slowing (delta/theta to alpha/sigma/beta power ratio) was associated with smaller nucleus basalis of Meynert volume, and smaller NbM volume was in turn associated with longer sleep latency and poorer episodic memory.

papers.title: Effects of stellate ganglion block on postoperative sleep disturbance: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 randomized controlled trials (734 participants) found that stellate ganglion block was associated with improved subjective sleep scores at multiple postoperative time points, including a standardized mean difference of -2.27 on postoperative day 1, and increased total sleep time by approximately 72 minutes. Heterogeneity was substantial for some outcomes, and the authors call for larger multicenter trials.

papers.title: Machine learning-based source-level EEG functional network biomarkers of antidepressant treatment response in major depressive disorder.
papers.summary: Baseline resting-state EEG source-level functional networks were analyzed in 47 patients with major depressive disorder and 41 healthy controls; non-responders to 12-week antidepressants showed lower strength and clustering coefficient and higher path length in the high beta band than responders. A support vector machine using nodal network features classified responders versus non-responders with 82.98% accuracy, and theta-band eigenvector centrality in the precuneus and pars orbitalis correlated with psychological assessment scores in responders.

papers.title: Within-cohort discrimination and cross-cohort transfer of EEG-based ADHD classifiers: An exploratory two-cohort evaluation
papers.summary: An exploratory two-cohort reanalysis found that EEG-based ADHD classifiers using Cz/F4, 128 Hz data showed strong within-cohort balanced accuracy in adults (spectral models ~0.95) but not in children (~0.55-0.57), and cross-cohort transfer produced reverse ranking with AUCs mostly below 0.5.

papers.title: Associations between weather variables and sleep architecture: A large-scale analysis using consumer sleep data.
papers.summary: Analyzing 236,115 nights of home-based sleep data from 1,067 users in South Korea, higher temperature was associated with decreased sleep efficiency and total sleep time and increased sleep latency, while longer sunshine duration was linked to greater total sleep time and REM sleep ratio. Temperature and sunshine duration interacted with apnea-hypopnea index group, with weather-associated changes in sleep efficiency, total sleep time, and wake after sleep onset diminished in nights with higher AHI.

papers.title: Pre-stroke sleep symptoms and neurological outcomes after stroke: an exploratory secondary analysis of two prospective cohorts.
papers.summary: In an exploratory secondary analysis of 133 stroke patients from two prospective cohorts, pre-stroke unintended leg movements, sleep-maintenance insomnia, and nocturia were associated with higher follow-up NIHSS scores, while hypnagogic hallucinations were linked to worse admission outcomes including higher NIHSS and lower Barthel Index.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Association between Neurovascular Network Dysfunction and Poor Sleep Quality in Patients with Cerebral Small Vessel Disease.
papers.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional analysis of 102 cerebral small vessel disease patients, exploratory associations were found between poor sleep quality (PSQI>5) and multidomain neurovascular network measures (autonomic, haemodynamic, neuroelectrical), but none survived FDR correction; a multidomain model showed an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.758.

papers.title: Tsmd-net: two-stage multi-domain distillation network for cross-subject MI-EEG domain generalization.
papers.summary: The study proposes TSMD-Net, a two-stage multi-domain distillation network for cross-subject motor imagery EEG domain generalization, achieving mean accuracies of 70.21%, 77.82%, and 79.53% on BCI Competition IV 2a, 2b, and High Gamma Dataset, respectively.

papers.title: AI-enabled passive digital phenotyping of experiential negative symptoms in schizophrenia-spectrum disorders: a narrative review on the path from sensing to clinical endpoints.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on AI-enabled passive digital phenotyping for experiential negative symptoms in schizophrenia-spectrum disorders, proposing a construct-to-endpoint pipeline and highlighting that current single-modality correlations are modest and insufficient for valid digital endpoints.

papers.title: Wearables for Physical Activity Guideline Development and Health Surveillance: Converging Research and Practice Agendas.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines the convergence of wearable-based methods for physical activity surveillance and etiological epidemiology, contrasting WHO standardization with the Prospective Physical Activity, Sitting, and Sleep consortium. It outlines a 10-year roadmap for a globally harmonized wearable evidence ecosystem, noting that wearables capture high-resolution activity dimensions and have identified strong dose-response associations at lower volumes than current guidelines.

papers.title: Risk factors for pulmonary mortality in patients with obstructive sleep apnea: a competing risk analysis integrating Cox regression, random survival forests, and unsupervised clustering.
papers.summary: In 4368 OSA patients, a competing risk analysis integrating Cox regression, random survival forests, and clustering identified age, nocturnal desaturation, active smoking, BMI, and male sex as independent predictors of pulmonary mortality (101 deaths); the RSF C-index was 0.84 and four phenotypes were found, with the highest-risk cluster reaching ~8% 20-year pulmonary mortality.

papers.title: The influence of temperature on suicidality in youth: The role of insomnia.
papers.journal: The journal of climate change and health
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional analysis of 5,590 pediatric psychiatric emergency patients, mean and minimum daily temperatures moderated the temperature-suicidality relationship only in those with insomnia (RR 1.06 per 5°C), and minimum temperature was associated with suicidality through insomnia in a mediation model (OR 1.05).

papers.title: Sleep-related metrics that predict training intensity: an exploratory study in women's college athletics.
papers.journal: Frontiers in sports and active living
papers.summary: This two-week observational study of 13 women's college athletes characterized daily heart rate- and perception-based markers of exertion using WHOOP monitors and RPE. Linear mixed-effects models showed that worse average sleep was associated with higher HR-based exertion, while within-person elevations in sleep consistency and greater average sleep need were linked to higher HR-based exertion and lower perceived exertion.

papers.title: Deletion of Cipc promotes regenerative myogenesis in mdx mice and is associated with increased myogenin expression.
papers.summary: Satellite cell-specific deletion of Cipc in mdx mice increased centrally nucleated fibers, embryonic myosin heavy chain-positive regenerating fibers, and MyHC-positive myotubes in primary cultures. Cipc deletion was accompanied by increased MyoD and myogenin expression and increased p38 and ELK-1 phosphorylation, suggesting a candidate p38/ELK-1-myogenin axis in regenerative myogenesis.

papers.title: Quantitative FP-CIT PET analysis of dopaminergic degeneration in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder and early Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: Quantitative 18F-FP-CIT PET analysis of 33 healthy controls, 77 iRBD patients, and 194 early PD patients revealed stepwise reductions in striatal SUVRs (HC > iRBD > early PD), with putaminal asymmetry elevated only in early PD and A-P ratios differing among all groups. Putamen SUVR and A-P ratio predicted phenoconversion in iRBD comparably to expert visual interpretation.

papers.title: Electroencephalography research in neuropathic pain (Review).
papers.summary: This narrative review integrates mechanistic and electrophysiological evidence on EEG alterations in neuropathic pain, highlighting recurrent resting-state theta increases and dominant-frequency slowing, while alpha, beta, and gamma findings remain heterogeneous; network analyses reveal aberrant prefrontal-limbic and sensorimotor connectivity.

papers.title: Decoding melatonin's role in musculoskeletal health: mechanistic foundations and clinical applications.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes experimental, translational, and clinical evidence on melatonin's roles in musculoskeletal health, detailing mechanisms such as MT1/MT2 receptor signaling, Wnt/β-catenin stabilization, antioxidant and mitochondrial effects, and epigenetic regulation across bone, cartilage, muscle, tendon, ligament, and spine. It concludes that melatonin shows therapeutic promise but translation requires precision dosing, improved bioavailability, and large-scale validation.

papers.title: Correction: Unveiling the inflammatory link: integrated analysis identifies BMP7 and PPBP as key genes in obstructive sleep apnea-related atrial fibrillation.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This is a correction notice for an article that identified BMP7 and PPBP as key genes in obstructive sleep apnea-related atrial fibrillation through integrated analysis.

papers.title: Reduced 24-hour heart rate variability in neurosyphilis: a retrospective case-control study.
papers.summary: In a retrospective case-control study of 98 neurosyphilis patients and 53 controls, neurosyphilis was associated with 15.3% lower 24-hour SDNN and reduced vagally mediated heart rate variability, with nighttime RMSSD increases being smaller in patients.

papers.title: Electroencephalography for Radiation-Free Orientation Estimation of Directional Deep Brain Stimulation Leads
papers.summary: The study developed and evaluated a radiation-free EEG framework for estimating the orientation of directional deep brain stimulation leads using a realistic head phantom and postoperative human data. The tri-montage approach reduced orientation error to 0.59° in the phantom, and in a patient, EEG-derived orientations differed from imaging-based references by about 8° and 15° for the right and left leads, respectively, demonstrating the feasibility of EEG-based orientation estimation.

papers.title: A Series of N-of-1 Trials Characterizing Individual Responses to Theta-Burst Stimulation in Post-traumatic Trigeminal Neuropathic Pain.
papers.summary: A series of N-of-1 trials in eight patients with post-traumatic trigeminal neuropathic pain found heterogeneous individual responses to theta-burst stimulation, with pain intensity decreasing in some patients but no consistent treatment-specific pattern compared to sham stimulation.

papers.title: Anti-KLHL11 antibody encephalitis without detectable malignancy: a case report and literature review.
papers.summary: This case report and literature review analyzed 13 cases of anti-KLHL11 antibody encephalitis without detectable malignancy. The most common manifestations were ataxia, dysarthria, and gaze palsy/nystagmus; after immunotherapy, 6 patients improved, 3 remained stable, 4 deteriorated, and 2 died, suggesting that clinical symptoms and neuroimaging cannot reliably distinguish these from tumor-positive cases.

papers.title: Study protocol for a randomized controlled trial comparing penetrating needling and cognitive behavioral therapy for subjective tinnitus.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a randomized controlled trial to evaluate penetrating needling versus cognitive behavioral therapy for subjective tinnitus in 72 participants, with primary outcomes including the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory and Tinnitus Questionnaire.

papers.title: Management of recurrent posterior dislocation of a stock temporomandibular joint prosthesis using class II elastic traction: A case report and literature review.
papers.summary: A case report of recurrent posterior dislocation after stock temporomandibular joint replacement managed successfully with class II elastic traction, and a literature review of 10 publications involving 57 patients with perioperative prosthesis dislocation.

papers.title: Kidney Transplant Recipients' Experiences of Sleep and Coping Strategies: An Interpretative Phenomenological Study.
papers.summary: Interpretative phenomenological study of 12 kidney transplant recipients identified four themes: disrupted nighttime sleep, emotional distress, social support, and self-adjustment strategies. It reports that sleep disturbances are intertwined with emotional well-being and coping, supporting individualized post-transplant sleep and psychosocial care.

papers.title: Self-management strategies for menstrual cycle symptoms: a systematic review.
papers.summary: Systematic review of 39 randomized controlled trials (3,806 participants) evaluated non-clinical self-management strategies for menstrual cycle symptoms. Physical activity, especially yoga, and nutritional strategies (vitamin and mineral supplementation) predominantly improved symptoms such as discomfort, fatigue, and mood, though evidence was limited by small samples and methodological inconsistencies.

papers.title: Cortical Spreading Depression Mimicking Ischemic Stroke: A Case Report of Complex Hemiplegic Migraine with Reversible Cortical Magnetic Resonance Imaging Changes.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 66-year-old man with hemiplegic migraine presenting with acute left-sided hemiparesis and stroke-like MRI findings, including diffusion-weighted hyperintensities without corresponding ADC reduction. The patient improved gradually over 7 days, highlighting the importance of recognizing hemiplegic migraine as a stroke mimic and using MRI ADC status to differentiate from acute ischemic stroke.

papers.title: Narrative nursing for prolonged myelosuppression after autologous stem cell transplantation in multiple myeloma: A case report.
papers.summary: Case report of a 46-year-old man with multiple myeloma who developed prolonged myelosuppression, febrile neutropenia, and oral mucositis after autologous stem cell transplantation. Individualized narrative nursing during a 16-day hospitalization was associated with resolution of fever and mucositis, hematopoietic recovery, and improved emotional adjustment and treatment engagement.

papers.title: Mothers' perceptions and decision-making regarding tandem breastfeeding in Türkiye: a child health-focused qualitative study.
papers.summary: Qualitative study of 21 mothers in Türkiye used reflexive thematic analysis to explore perceptions and decision-making about tandem breastfeeding. Four themes emerged: perceived meaning, perceived burden, social perceptions, and limited professional support; mothers associated the practice with maintaining mother-child bonds and preventing abrupt weaning but also with fatigue and uncertainty.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
